articles.title: Palestinian child killed by Israeli gunfire in northern Gaza
articles.summary:
Palestinian child killed by Israeli gunfire in northern Gaza

A seven-year-old Palestinian child succumbed to his wounds on Sunday after being shot by Israeli forces in Jabalia refugee camp, north of the Gaza Strip, Wafa news reported.

Medical sources told Wafa and Al Jazeera that Jihad al-Ghandour died from injuries sustained on Saturday when Israeli forces shot him near al-Houja Street in Jabalia camp.

Medical sources announced earlier that the death toll from the Israeli genocide in Gaza since 7 October 2023 had risen to 74,377, with 175,398 Palestinians injured.

articles.title: Former US official says Israeli demands made Gaza deal 'impossible for another six months'
articles.summary:
Former US official says Israeli demands made Gaza deal 'impossible for another six months'

A former senior US official has accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of delaying a captive exchange and ceasefire deal in Gaza in 2024 by "so many of his own conditions", which prevented an agreement for "another six months".

Phil Gordon, who served as national security adviser to former US Vice President Kamala Harris from March 2022 to January 2025, made the allegations in a post on X on Saturday.

“Netanyahu instead added so many of his own conditions - against the advice of his own security chiefs - that the deal became impossible for another six months,” Gordon wrote. 

He said nearly 9,000 more Palestinians were killed in that period and more Israeli captives died. 

Gordon said the added Israeli demands included keeping forces along Gaza’s entire border with Egypt and a new mechanism to screen Palestinians returning north.

Both were dropped in the deal finally concluded in January 2025.

Read more: Former US official says Israeli demands made Gaza deal 'impossible for another six months'

articles.title: Senior military commander says Iran will continue to strike vessels ‘if necessary’
articles.summary:
Senior military commander says Iran will continue to strike vessels ‘if necessary’

Iranian forces will continue to strike vessels in the Strait of Hormuz “if necessary”, senior Iranian military commander and deputy army coordinator Habibollah Sayyari said on Sunday. 

“We have dealt blows to enemy vessels, and if something happens against Iran again, we will strike at them. We are not tied, and we have facilities and capabilities that are specific and general in the world,” he said in comments carried by Iranian media.

articles.summary: The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize has exposed two political universes: a South Africa that defies imperial power and Israeli impunity, and a nuclear-armed Pakistan whose prime minister has elevated subservience into an instrument of statecraft. Íránské síly pokračují v ohrožování námořní dopravy, zatímco v Izraeli roste kybernetická hranice hrozeb po zneužití bezpečnostních kamer k sledování vojenských cílů. Diplomatické snahy o rozšíření Abrahámových dohod a řešení konfliktu v Gaze se potýkají s výraznými překážkami.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region remains critical due to ongoing military operations in Gaza and escalating maritime incidents in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. Iranian forces continue to threaten shipping lanes, while Israel faces a heightened cyber threat landscape following the compromise of security cameras to track military targets. Diplomatic efforts regarding Abraham Accords expansion and a Gaza resolution continue to face severe roadblocks.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující napětí v Perském zálivu kolem námořní bezpečnosti, přetrvávající operace v Gaze a zvýšená kybernetická opatření v Izraeli.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued tensions in the Persian Gulf regarding maritime security, ongoing operations in Gaza, and heightened cyber-security measures in Israel are expected.
